632.description: Plain mats make a loose, unfinished circle around untouched cups. The place at the head is empty, and faint footprints lead out through the doorway. These traces are imagined, not evidence of a gathering here.

labels.title: An unfinished circle
labels.inRoom: The mats do not form a settled arrangement, and the cups are untouched. This gathering is imagined.
labels.inRecord: After Muhammad died in 632, members of the community held different views about who should lead it.

labels.title: A place left empty
labels.inRoom: There is no person or seat at the head of this imagined circle. No such empty place is documented.
labels.inRecord: Abu Bakr became the first caliph. Supporters of Ali understood rightful leadership through Muhammad's family.

labels.title: Footprints toward the doorway
labels.inRoom: Faint footprints suggest departure from this invented room. They do not trace a documented journey.
labels.inRecord: Before Muhammad's burial, some companions met at Saqifa to choose a successor. Abu Bakr was selected as caliph.

661.description: In the 661 version of the imagined room, mats face one plain seat. A sealed letter and an interpretive coin replica sit on a low table. Empty pegs leave pale outlines by the door. This arrangement is invented, not a record of a particular room.

labels.title: Mats facing one seat
labels.inRoom: The rearranged mats and plain seat are invented. This is not a documented seat of power or a throne.
labels.inRecord: After Ali's death in 661, Mu'awiya became caliph and based his rule in Damascus.

labels.title: A sealed letter
labels.inRoom: The sealed letter is invented. It is not a surviving message or evidence that an official visited this room.
labels.inRecord: Early Arabic sources credit Mu'awiya with a chancellery and postal service during his reign, intended to improve communication. The source does not date their creation to 661.

labels.title: An interpretive coin replica
labels.inRoom: The coin is a modern interpretive replica, not a find from this imagined room or a photograph of the museum coin.
labels.inRecord: The British Museum catalogs an Arab-Sasanian silver coin minted at Nihavand in 660 CE. Its accession number is 1922,0424.3865.

labels.title: Empty pegs by the door
labels.inRoom: The pale outlines and empty pegs are invented. No belongings or departure from this room are documented.
labels.inRecord: Ali's rule from 656 to 661 was contested, and civil war followed before Mu'awiya became caliph.
